doc.name: A — haircare catalogue, ingredient scatter, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: argan oil hair treatment pump
Category: haircare
Shot programme: ingredient scatter
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium haircare product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the extreme wide set in an ingredient scatter treatment.

SUBJECT. A argan oil hair treatment pump. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Wide frame with the product small in a large, deliberately empty set. Shoot on a 24mm wide at f/2.8, framing for leading lines converging on the subject from the lower corners.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a hair light and background separation light with the key pulled two stops down. Stage the product on or against cast pigmented resin, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a clean high-key grade with the whites pushed to the edge of clipping. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
